text:
An electron (of mass m) and a photon have the same energy E in the range of a few eV. The ratio
of the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron and the wavelength of the photon is (c
= speed of light in vaccuum)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$λ_{e}$ = $\frac{h}{p_{e}}$ = $\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$

E = $\frac{hc}{λ_{photon}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ_{photon}$ = $\frac{hc}{E}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{λ_{e}}{λ_{photon}}$ = $\frac{1}{c}\left (\frac{E}{2m}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
Mass per unit area of a circular disc of radius $a$ depends on the distance r from its centre as $σ(r)$ = A + Br
. The moment of inertia of the disc about the axis, perpendicular to the plane and
passing through its centre is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$dI = dm(r^{2})$

and dm = $σ$2$π$rdr

$\therefore$ dI = $σ$2$π$rdr$(r^{2}) =$ $σ$2$πr^{3}dr$

Given $σ(r)$ = A + Br

$\therefore$ dI = 2$π(A + Br)r^{3}dr$

$\int dI=\int\limits _{0}^{a}2πr^{3}(A+Br)dr$

$\Rightarrow$ I = $2π\left [\frac{Ar^{4}}{4}+\frac{Br^{5}}{5}\right ]$

= $2πa^{4}\left (\frac{A}{4}+\frac{aB}{5}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
A particle of mass m and charge q has an initial velocity $\vec{v}=v_{0}\hat{j}$
. If an electric field $\vec{E}=E_{0}\hat{i}$
 and
magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_{0}\hat{i}$
 act on the particle, its speed will double after a time:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electric force $qE_{0}\hat{i}$ gives a constant acceleration $\dfrac{qE_{0}}{m}$ along x, so $v_{x}=\dfrac{qE_{0}}{m}t$.

The magnetic force $q⃗{v}\times B_{0}\hat{i}$ has no x-component, so it does not change $v_{x}$. It is perpendicular to $⃗{v}$, so it does no work and only rotates the velocity component in the y-z plane, whose magnitude stays $v_{0}$.

Hence $v^{2}=v_{x}^{2}+v_{0}^{2}$. For $v=2v_{0}$:

$v_{x}^{2}=4v_{0}^{2}-v_{0}^{2}\Rightarrow v_{x}=\sqrt{3}v_{0}$

$\dfrac{qE_{0}}{m}t=\sqrt{3}v_{0}\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}mv_{0}}{qE_{0}}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

$\therefore$ $\frac{i_{\infty }}{i_{40s}}$ = $\frac{i_{0}}{i_{0}\left (1-e^{-\dfrac{5\times 40}{10\times 10-3}}\right )}$

 = $\frac{1}{(1-e^{-2000})}$ $\approx$ 1

text:
A planar loop of wire rotates in a uniform magnetic field. Initially at t = 0, the plane of the loop
is perpendicular to the magnetic field. If it rotates with a period of 10 s about an axis in its plane
then the magnitude of induced emf will be maximum and minimum, respectively at :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $t=0$ the plane of the loop is perpendicular to $⃗{B}$, so the area vector is along $⃗{B}$ and the flux at time $t$ is

$𝜙=BA\cos ωt,ω=\frac{2π}{T},T=10\text{s}$

The induced emf is

$e=-\frac{d𝜙}{dt}=BAω\sin ωt$

$|e|$ is maximum when $\sin ωt=\pm 1$, i.e. $ωt=\dfrac{π}{2},\dfrac{3π}{2}$, giving $t=\dfrac{T}{4},\dfrac{3T}{4}=2.5\text{s},7.5\text{s}$.

$|e|$ is minimum (zero) when $\sin ωt=0$, i.e. $ωt=nπ$, giving $t=\dfrac{nT}{2}=0,5\text{s},10\text{s}$.

Only option (D) pairs a maximum (2.5 s) with a minimum (5.0 s); option (A) gives two maxima, option (B) two minima, and option (C) has the order reversed.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
Under an adiabatic process, the volume of an ideal gas gets doubled. Consequently the mean
collision time between the gas molecule changes from $τ_{1}$
 to $τ_{2}$
. If $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}=γ$ for this gas then a good
estimate for $\frac{τ_{2}}{τ_{1}}$
 is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mean free path is $λ=\dfrac{V}{\sqrt{2}πd^{2}N}$, so for a fixed number of molecules $λ\propto V$. The mean speed of the molecules is $\bar{v}\propto \sqrt{T}$. The mean collision time is therefore

$τ=\dfrac{λ}{\bar{v}}\propto \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{T}}$

For an adiabatic process, $TV^{γ-1}=\text{constant}$, so $T\propto V^{1-γ}$ and $\sqrt{T}\propto V^{\frac{1-γ}{2}}$.

Substituting,

$τ\propto V^{1-\frac{1-γ}{2}}=V^{\frac{1+γ}{2}}$

With the volume doubled,

$\dfrac{τ_{2}}{τ_{1}}=(2)^{\frac{1+γ}{2}}$

The expansion lengthens the collision time, so the ratio is greater than 1, unlike $\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{\frac{1+γ}{2}}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of 10 persons, with the average mass of each
person being 68 kg. The mass of the elevator itself is 920 kg and it moves with a constant speed
of 3 m/s. The frictional force opposing the motion is 6000 N. If the elevator is moving up with its
full capacity, the power delivered by the motor to the elevator $(g = 10 m/s^{2})$ must be at least :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Net force on motor will be

$F_{m} =$ [920 + 68(10)]g + 6000
= 22000 N

So, required power for motor

$P = F_{m}.V = 22000\times$3 = 66000 W
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
A thin lens made of glass (refractive index = 1.5) of focal length f = 16 cm is immersed in a liquid
of refractive index 1.42. If its focal length in liquid is $f_{1}$
, then the ratio $\frac{f_{1}}{f}$ is closest to the
integer :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using formula

$\frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{μ_{2}}{μ_{1}}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

$\frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{1.5}{1}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$ ...(1)

and $\frac{1}{f_{1}}=\left (\frac{1.5}{1.42}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$ ...(2)

Dividing (1) by (2), we get

$\frac{f_{1}}{f}=\frac{0.5}{0.056}$ = 8.93 $\approx$ 9
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by

$\vec{E}=E_{0}\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\cos (kz+ωt)$

At t = 0, a positively charged particle is at the point (x, y, z) = $\left (0,0,\frac{π}{k}\right )$.

 If its instantaneous velocity at
(t = 0) is $v_{0}\widehat{k}$
, the force acting on it due to the wave is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{E}=E_{0}\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\cos (kz+ωt)$

$\vec{E}$ at t = 0 at z = $\frac{π}{k}$ is given by

$\vec{E}=E_{0}\left (\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\cos \left (k\frac{π}{k}+ω(0)\right )$

= $-E_{0}\left (\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$

As $\vec{E}\times \vec{B}=\vec{c}$

Force due to magnetic field is in direction $q\left (\vec{v}\times \vec{B}\right )$ and given $\vec{v}$ parallel to  $\widehat{k}$.

$\vec{F}=$ $q\left (\vec{E}+\vec{v}\times \vec{B}\right )$

$\therefore$ $\vec{F}$ is in direction of $\vec{E}$

which is antiparallel to $\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
The sum of two forces $\vec{P}$
 and $\vec{Q}$
 is $\vec{R}$
 such that $\left |\vec{R}\right |=\left |\vec{P}\right |$
. The angle $θ$ (in degrees) that the
resultant of 2$\vec{P}$
and $\vec{Q}$
 will make with $\vec{Q}$
 is ..............
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $⃗{R}=⃗{P}+⃗{Q}$ and $|⃗{R}|=|⃗{P}|$:

$|⃗{P}+⃗{Q}|^{2}=|⃗{P}|^{2}\Rightarrow P^{2}+2⃗{P}\cdot ⃗{Q}+Q^{2}=P^{2}\Rightarrow 2⃗{P}\cdot ⃗{Q}+Q^{2}=0$

The dot product of the resultant of $2⃗{P}$ and $⃗{Q}$ with $⃗{Q}$ is

$(2⃗{P}+⃗{Q})\cdot ⃗{Q}=2⃗{P}\cdot ⃗{Q}+Q^{2}=0$

So $2⃗{P}+⃗{Q}$ is perpendicular to $⃗{Q}$, and $θ=90^{\circ }$.

Hence, the answer is 90.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
A 60 pF capacitor is fully charged by a 20 V supply. It is then disconnected from the supply and
is conneced to another uncharged 60 pF capacitor in parallel. The electrostatic energy that is lost
in this process by the time the charge is redistributed between them is (in $nJ) _____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$U_{i} =$ $\frac{1}{2}CV_{0}^{2}$

$U_{f} =$ $\frac{1}{2}\times 2C\times \left (\frac{V_{0}}{2}\right )^{2}$

$\Delta$E = $\frac{1}{2}CV_{0}^{2}$ - $\frac{1}{2}\times 2C\times \left (\frac{V_{0}}{2}\right )^{2}$

= $\frac{CV_{0}^{2}}{4}$

= $\frac{1}{4}\times 60\times 10^{-12}\times 4\times 10^{2}$

= 6 $\times$ $10^{-9} = 6 nJ$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot
